title_he: בֹּא אֶל־גּוֹאֵל הָאָדָם, הוֹי צְבָא אֲדֹנָי
review: 1:1–7 is the printed seven-line refrain stanza, with the two clauses repeated three times and the 'crowned' acclamation doubled inside it; the payload reproduces the repetition line for line (including the triple נִלְבַּשׁ) because that repetition is the tune, and shortening it would break the 86.86 – 66.66.6.67.66.6 shape.

3:2 גְּבֹר וְאַל־תֵּחָת — the Arabic فَاغْلِبْ وَلَا تَجْزَعْ is 'conquer and do not be dismayed'; חָתַת is the verb used in Deut 1:21 / Josh 1:9 (אַל־תֵּחָת), the same 'do not be shattered' of the conquest charge, so the army language stays coherent.

3:4 תִּנָּשֵׂא — the Arabic غَدًا يُنْزَع is 'tomorrow it is removed'; the Hebrew uses נָשָׂא in the sense of taking away (Isa 53:8, נִגְזַר) rather than 'lifted up', since the Arabic's verb is removal and the subject is the tear.
4:2 לַנִּכְנָע — the Arabic مَنْ يَخْضَع is 'whoever submits'; the Niphal participle is kept so the condition is submission itself, not humility as a character trait.

4:4 וְיִכְלֶה הַדֶּמַע — the Arabic وَيَنْتَهِي الْمَدْمَع is 'the weeping ends'; the Hebrew keeps the singular collective דֶּמַע (as in Jer 9:17, דִּמְעָה) with the verb of Ps 69:4, and pairs it with the opening 'war ends', so the stanza closes the same door the refrain opened.
